title: CS KPI Stencil: Latency, Uptime, Cost/Token, Cache-Hit Playbook
summary: Practical stencil for QBRs: concise definitions for latency, uptime, cost/token and cache hit rate plus a small ops checklist and a sample KPI table customers can adopt during renewal conversations.
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, repeatable KPI stencil for Customer Success QBRs. It defines the four metrics we surface most often in renewal conversations (latency, uptime, cost/token, cache hit rate), gives pragmatic measurement rules, suggested thresholds (signal/alert/renewal flags), and provides a one-page KPI table you can paste into customer decks.

Intended audience:
- CSMs preparing QBRs or renewal decks
- Solutions/SEs who need to explain performance economics
- Customer engineering contacts who request metric definitions

Notes-to-self: keep this short and repeatable. Customers want interpretable signals, not engineering minutiae. If they want the raw query we can attach an appendix.

1) Metric definitions (concise)
- Latency (tail & median): measured as server-side generation time excluding client-side network. We report p50, p95, p99 in milliseconds for standard prompt template families. Use rolling 7-day windows for trending, 30d for SLA context.
  - p50: median token generation latency per request (ms). Good for typical UX.
  - p95: 95th percentile latency — indicates tail experience and buffering needs.
  - p99: 99th percentile latency — critical for high-SLA customers or low-latency flows.

- Uptime (availability): percent of successful request completions over total requests that reached our platform gateway, measured per calendar month. Exclude scheduled maintenance windows and region-level provider outages (annotated). Uptime = (successful_completions - excluded) / (total_gateway_requests - excluded) * 100.
  - Success criteria: HTTP 2xx + streamed tokens completed.
  - Failure examples: timeouts, 5xx runtime errors, model OOMs returning error.

- Cost per token (normalized): net compute + infra cost divided by output tokens generated, reported in USD per 1,000 output tokens to keep numbers readable. We calculate using the accounting window for the customer (monthly). Include dedicated capacity amortization for Dedicated customers if applicable.
  - Note: upstream model size and quantization affect unit cost; present relative comparisons (e.g., gpt-like-large vs quantized-8bit) instead of raw single numbers when customers prefer conceptual view.

- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV combined): fraction of requests where we served one or more tokens from cache (prefix or KV) instead of fresh compute. Measured as: cached_requests / total_requests. Also capture token-level cache efficiency: cached_output_tokens / total_output_tokens.
  - Prefix hit: cache matched in first N tokens (configurable).
  - KV cache hit: internal KV-store reused during decode for multi-step dialogues/long-context reuse.

2) Measurement windows & data sources
- Standard windows: 7d (short), 30d (default QBR), 90d (trend/seasonality).
- Primary sources:
  - Redwood Console telemetry (latency percentiles, cache metrics)
  - Billing export for cost attribution (billing-YYYY-MM.csv)
  - Logs/traces for failure breakdowns (linked in appendix when requested)

3) Suggested thresholds and renewal signals (operationalized)
- Green / Acceptable:
  - p95 latency <= 600 ms for interactive apps; p99 <= 1200 ms
  - Monthly uptime >= 99.9%
  - Cost per 1k tokens within customer baseline +/- 15% of last quarter
  - Cache hit rate >= 30% for typical prompt-heavy agents
- Yellow / Monitor:
  - p95 between 600–1000 ms or p99 between 1200–2500 ms
  - Monthly uptime between 99.5%–99.9%
  - Cost drift >15% due to unanticipated token volume or model change
  - Cache hit rate between 10%–30% (opportunity for prompt engineering)
- Red / Renewal risk flag:
  - p99 > 2500 ms consistently or visible user impact
  - Monthly uptime < 99.5% or repeated region-level incidents
  - Cost per 1k tokens > 40% above baseline without feature benefit
  - Cache hit rate < 10% for workloads that should cache (calls with repeated prefixes)

Operational guidance: any red-level signal should trigger an action plan and be documented in the renewal playbook section.

4) One-page KPI table (copy-paste into QBR deck)
- Use the template below in the deck; replace bracketed fields with customer-specific values and add a 1–2 sentence implication and next-step.

KPI | Window | Current | Target | Trend | Notes
----|--------|---------|--------|-------|------
Latency p50 | 30d | [xx ms] | <= [target] | [up/down] | Typical user flow: [chat/api] 
Latency p95 | 30d | [xx ms] | <= [target] | [up/down] | Tail influenced by seq len/model
Uptime | 30d | [99.x%] | >= 99.9% | [stable/incident] | Last incident: [date], impact: [x mins] 
Cost per 1k tokens | 30d | [$x.xx] | <= $[target] | [up/down] | Includes caching & batching effects
Cache hit rate (req-level) | 30d | [xx%] | >= [target%] | [up/down] | Opportunity: [embed/cs suggestion]

Example row (fictional):
Latency p95 | 30d | 720 ms | <= 600 ms | up 10% | Increase due to long-context API calls after product change

5) Renewal playbook (cheat-sheet)
- If cost drift > threshold: 1) show token-level distribution (top 5 flows), 2) propose batching/caching knobs and model-variant plan (quantized alternative + same prompt), 3) commit to pilot with metrics and timeline.
- If latency tail shows degradation: 1) identify top N routes contributing to p95/p99, 2) propose canary fallback to faster model variant for critical route, 3) enable auto-fallback policy for burst windows.
- If uptime incidents: 1) produce RCA with SRE and share within 72 hours, 2) propose SLA credit / dedicated capacity if incident pattern repeats, 3) review routing/fallback policy.

6) Quick queries & artifacts to attach (for engineering appendix)
- Console queries: latency p95 by route, 7d and 30d.
- Billing: cost-per-route and cost-per-model breakdown.
- Cache: token-level hit table by route and by prompt hash.
(We keep these in appendix; paste raw queries on request.)

7) Checklist for the slide + pre-QBR prep
- [ ] Pull 30d and 90d snapshots for the table
- [ ] Annotate any incidents affecting uptime in the last 90d
- [ ] Run cost delta analysis vs prior quarter and explain major drivers
- [ ] Identify 1–2 prioritized ops recommendations (owner + timeline)
- [ ] Draft a short ‘asks’ section for customer (e.g., enable caching, reduce max tokens)

8) Talking points (30–60s soundbites)
- Latency: "Most of your users see median responses under [x]ms; a small tail of complex requests drives perceived slowness — we recommend a canary fallback for those routes."
- Cost: "We can reduce unit cost by X% through quantized model variant + cache policy; we'll run a 2-week pilot and measure token-level savings."
- Cache: "Your agent pattern is cache-friendly — a 30% hit rate is realistic with modest prompt deduping. We can add a quick plugin to improve that within one sprint."

Open questions / TODOs
- Agree on canonical cost-per-token definition for Dedicated vs Hosted: do we show amortized Dedicated cost or exclude infra fixed costs? (CS-482)
- Add standard snippet for proof-of-savings pilot (template SOW).

Appendix (links)
- Confluence: QBR templates and older playbooks (pageId=12345)
- Jira: CS-482 (cost definition debate)
- Sample billing export: billing-2024-01.csv (stored in shared drive)

Raw notes (working):
- Keep examples short. Customer decks prefer 1 slide per metric with clear implication and next-step.
- Ops teams love thresholds expressed as boolean checks (green/yellow/red) — include these in the appendix per-customer.

End of stencil.

Author note: Hannah added the initial threshold numbers based on recent renewals; Luis validated the billing mapping. We'll iterate after 2 QBRs and shorten the table if customers ask for less detail.
